subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Is fail-closed rejection of every legacy ownerless session the intended upgrade boundary for plugin-runtime callers, with operator or non-plugin recovery as the only supported path?
rationale: An ownerless row has no safely inferable plugin authority, but unconditional rejection can stop previously working plugin-runtime mutations after an upgrade, so security and compatibility intent must be explicit.

options.title: Approve strict ownership
options.body: Require an exact stored-owner match, document operator recovery for ownerless rows, and retain the current fail-closed implementation.

options.title: Require a migration
options.body: Add a narrow migration only for rows whose historical plugin ownership can be verified without allowing arbitrary plugin adoption.

recommendation.title: Approve strict ownership
recommendation.body: Require an exact stored-owner match, document operator recovery for ownerless rows, and retain the current fail-closed implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged memory-core lifecycle work is the closest identified history for plugin-owned session creation, identity, and cleanup behavior.
